question.problem:
Consider the following system of linear equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned} & x+3z=1 \\  & y-2z=-1 \\  & z=2\end{aligned}
$$

Use the standard Gauss-Jordan method to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to reduced row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.
question.worked_solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 3 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}].
$$

Notice that the matrix $M$ is already in row echelon form.

Transforming $M$ to reduced row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 3 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+2{R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 3 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+(-3){R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 & -5 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding system is now

$$
{\begin{aligned} & x=-5 \\  & y=3 \\  & z=2.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have the solution $x=-5$, $y=3$, and $z=2.$
